original_question: What are the Liouville-integrability and possible super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems Ṗ = Q(P) that arise from known Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors?
target_in_paper: The nearest target is the paper’s unlabeled open-problem cluster on the integrability and analytic properties of Kontsevich graph-symmetry flows, i.e. the PDE/integrable-systems questions that arise when a universal flow Pdot = Q(P) is restricted to concrete classes of Poisson brackets. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main dynamical object: nonlinear evolutionary equations of the form Pdot = Q(P) produced by known Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson bivectors, and it correctly recognizes that the paper is asking an integrability-type question about such flows rather than about the graph complex alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper does not formulate this problem specifically in Liouville- or super-integrability language; it asks more broadly about integrability and analytic properties of the induced symmetry flows. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))

Q(P) is not an arbitrary nonlinear operator: it is the universal flow obtained from a graph cocycle γ by Kontsevich’s orientation morphism, i.e. Q(P) = Or(γ)(P⊗n). ([preprints.ihes.fr](https://preprints.ihes.fr/storage/sqs1_.pdf))

The ambient geometric setting is that of Poisson bivectors on finite-dimensional real affine manifolds; your draft omits the finite-dimensional affine context. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))

In the paper’s intended PDE/integrability problem, one first restricts the universal flow to a concrete graph-stable class of Poisson brackets; only then does one obtain an explicit finite-order nonlinear PDE system for class parameters. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))

The nearest concrete formulation supplied by the author in immediate follow-up work is for Nambu-type brackets, where the flow evolves Casimirs and density; your draft does not mention that sort of parameterization, which is what makes the PDE question stand-alone. ([preprints.ihes.fr](https://preprints.ihes.fr/storage/sqs1_.pdf))

No Hamiltonian structure, involutive family of first integrals, symplectic/Poisson phase-space data, or dimensional count needed to state Liouville or super-integrability is specified in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))

A paper-faithful formulation should also avoid suggesting commuting symmetry flows: in the author’s concrete Nambu-type example, evolutions induced by different graph cocycles are explicitly noted not to commute. ([preprints.ihes.fr](https://preprints.ihes.fr/storage/sqs1_.pdf))
refined_question: For a known Kontsevich graph cocycle γ, with universal Poisson-bivector flow Pdot = Q(P) = Or(γ)(P⊗n) on finite-dimensional real affine Poisson manifolds, and for any concrete class of Poisson brackets that is preserved by this flow, determine whether the induced finite-order nonlinear evolution system for the class parameters is integrable, and describe its analytic properties (for example, after rewriting the flow in terms of Casimirs and density in graph-stable Nambu-type cases).
justification: The draft is closest to the paper’s PDE/integrable-systems open-problem cluster, but it is not fully paper-faithful because it sharpens the question into Liouville/super-integrability without the Hamiltonian data needed to make those notions precise. The abstract of 1910.05844 says the paper poses open problems about the integrability and analytic properties of the symmetry flows, and the author’s contemporaneous talk abstract based on that paper says this is the branch of the work dealing with PDE and integrable systems. The nearest concrete downstream formulation by the same author says that, for graph-stable Nambu-type Poisson brackets, the universal flow induces evolution equations for Casimirs and density and that “its integrability is an open problem,” while flows from different cocycles need not commute. That is why the refined question asks for integrability/analytic structure of the induced evolution system on preserved classes, rather than for Liouville or super-integrability in advance. Direct full-text access to 1910.05844 beyond the abstract was not available in the accessible mirror, so the non-abstract page placements below are best-effort reconstructions from contemporaneous abstracts and this immediate follow-up paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844?utm_source=openai))
